tldr: Motorola Solutions reported Q4 2025 sales of $3.38B (+12%) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.59 (+14%), closing FY2025 with $11.68B of sales (+8%), record operating cash flow, and record ending backlog of $15.7B. Management guided FY2026 revenue of about $12.7B and non-GAAP EPS of $16.70-$16.85, supported by strong orders, continued software and services growth, and a higher Silvus revenue outlook.
bullets: Q4 results were above guide with broad-based growth: sales of $3.38B (+12%), non-GAAP operating earnings of $1.09B (+19%), non-GAAP operating margin of 32.1% (+170 bps), and non-GAAP EPS of $4.59 (+14%); Q4 operating cash flow was $1.3B and free cash flow was $1.1B.

FY2025 results: sales of $11.68B (+8%), non-GAAP operating earnings of $3.54B (+13%), non-GAAP operating margin of 30.3% (+130 bps), and non-GAAP EPS of $15.38 (+11%); operating cash flow was a record $2.8B (+19%) and free cash flow was $2.6B (+21%).

Demand indicators and 2026 guide stayed strong: ending backlog reached a record $15.7B (+$1.0B YoY, +$1.2B QoQ) with Q4 orders up 26%; guidance calls for Q1 revenue growth of 6%-7% and non-GAAP EPS of $3.20-$3.25, and FY2026 revenue of about $12.7B with non-GAAP EPS of $16.70-$16.85.
participants: Jason Winkler (Executive Vice President and CFO)
Jack Molloy (Executive Vice President and COO)
Mahesh Saptharishi (Executive Vice President and CTO)
themes: Asset visibility and data capture adoption expanding
Portfolio shifts and M&A reshaping focus
Pricing and cost pressure shaping margins

segments.title: Products and Systems Integration
points: Q4 revenue was $2.16B (+11% YoY), driven by MCN and Video; non-GAAP operating earnings were $667M with 30.9% margin (+40 bps YoY).
FY2025 revenue was $7.25B (+5%) and non-GAAP operating earnings were $2.10B with 28.9% margin (+80 bps).

Q4 notable wins included a $180M P25 system expansion (Tennessee), a $162M U.S. federal P25 device/SVX order, an $81M TETRA system in North Africa, and a $20M Silvus order for an unmanned systems provider.

segments.title: Software and Services
points: Q4 revenue was $1.22B (+15% YoY) with growth across all three technologies; non-GAAP operating earnings were $419M and margin was 34.3% (+400 bps).
FY2025 revenue was $4.43B (+13%) and non-GAAP operating earnings were $1.44B with 32.5% margin (+170 bps).

Q4 wins included a $201M 10-year P25 services renewal (Maryland), an $86M international command center order, a $79M Prince George's County P25 services/command center order, and large TETRA service orders in the U.K. and Europe.

segments.title: Orders, backlog, and regional demand
points: Q4 orders grew 26% and ending backlog reached $15.7B (+$1.0B YoY, +$1.2B QoQ).
Software and Services backlog increased $1.4B YoY and $945M QoQ; Products and SI backlog was down $323M YoY (strong first-half LMR shipments) but up $235M QoQ on record Q4 MCN and Video orders.
Q4 regional revenue: North America $2.36B (+7%) and International $1.02B (+26%); FY2025 regional revenue: North America $8.36B (+7%) and International $3.32B (+11%).

segments.title: AI platform and portfolio execution
points: Management launched Dispatcher and Responder Assist Suites at $99 per user per month and positioned Assist as a recurring software growth driver tied to command center workflows.
APX Next subscribers reached more than 200,000 at end-2025 (target 300,000 by end-2026), while SVX shipments exceeded 15,000 units.
Silvus integration remained a major portfolio focus; management raised 2026 Silvus revenue expectation to $675M, up $75M versus the prior expectation.

guidance.label: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS
guidance.note: effective tax rate about 22.5%; 168M diluted shares

guidance.label: FY2026 segment growth
guidance.value: Software and Services 10% - 11%; Products and SI 7% - 8%
guidance.note: technology view: Video 10% - 11%, Command Center 15%, MCN 7% - 8%

notes.title: Capital allocation and balance sheet
points: FY2025 capital deployment included $4.9B of acquisitions (including Silvus), $1.2B of share repurchases, $728M of dividends, and $265M of capex.
The company repaid $200M of Silvus-related term loans after year-end, leaving $1.3B outstanding.

notes.title: Margin and cost bridge into 2026
points: Management guided to about 100 bps of operating margin expansion in 2026 despite an incremental tariff headwind of about $60M in 1H26 and expected memory cost increases.
Mitigation levers discussed were mix toward software/services, operating leverage, vendor actions, and selective pricing.

notes.title: Backlog normalization context
points: Management said more than half of revenue now follows a quick-turn profile (sold and installed within the same year) as product backlog normalizes from prior supply-chain distortion.
On Q&A, management said there was no residual benefit from repricing legacy pandemic backlog contracts.

themes.title: Silvus growth and defense/federal expansion
points: Management raised 2026 Silvus revenue expectations to $675M and cited continued demand from Ukraine, broader NATO programs, and unmanned systems.
Executives framed most near-term Silvus opportunity around defense, borders, and unmanned use cases, with state and local use cases more spectrum-dependent.

themes.title: 2026 margin outlook versus tariff and memory pressure
points: Management acknowledged about $60M of incremental tariff pressure in 1H26 and memory cost inflation but still guided to operating margin expansion.
The margin thesis emphasized richer mix in software/services, stronger device and application attach, and disciplined cost control.

themes.title: Backlog, order durability, and seasonality
points: Management said record Q4 product orders ($2.4B, up about $500M YoY) and a strong pipeline support confidence in 2026 guidance.
Product backlog is expected to decline seasonally in Q1, then recover, with management expecting double-digit product order growth in Q1 and for full-year 2026.

themes.title: Command Center and Assist Suite monetization
points: Management linked command center acceleration to APX Next subscriber growth and integrated AI workflows across 911, CAD, records, and responder tools.
Assist Suite pricing was positioned at $99 per user per month (incremental to radios), with contract-length flexibility and more feature releases expected through 2026.

top_questions.question: What is driving the higher Silvus outlook and how much is tied to federal and unmanned demand?
top_questions.summary: Management said Silvus execution since close has exceeded expectations and raised 2026 Silvus revenue guidance to $675M, with demand concentrated in Ukraine, NATO markets, and unmanned defense programs.

top_questions.question: How can margins expand in 2026 despite tariff and memory headwinds?
top_questions.summary: Management guided to about 100 bps operating margin expansion, citing mix shift toward software and services, operating leverage, and mitigation actions against about $60M of incremental tariffs and higher memory costs.

top_questions.question: Is current backlog and order strength sustainable as product backlog normalizes?
top_questions.summary: Management highlighted three consecutive quarters of double-digit product orders, expected another double-digit year in 2026, and said product backlog should be seasonally lower in Q1 before improving later in the year.

top_questions.question: How are Assist Suites being sold and what early traction is visible?
top_questions.summary: Assist Suites are sold at $99 per user per month and are incremental to radio hardware; management reported growing adoption across responder and dispatcher workflows and expects continued feature launches on a roughly quarterly cadence.

implications: Motorola is using integrated workflows (radio, video, command center, and AI Assist Suites) to raise software and services attach on an already large installed base.
Record backlog and sustained double-digit product order expectations suggest public safety and defense demand remains resilient despite backlog normalization dynamics.
Silvus plus FedRAMP milestones for APX Next, SVX, and digital evidence management expand MSI's ability to compete for federal and defense programs where secure, integrated platforms matter.
competitive_notes: Management explicitly positioned the $99 Assist Suite offer as more comprehensive and lower-cost versus alternatives, while emphasizing contract flexibility rather than long locked terms.
Video strategy combines cloud growth (Alta) with on-prem/hybrid pathways (Unity), which management said supports broader deployment flexibility by customer vertical.
forecast_hooks: Track APX Next subscriber progression from more than 200,000 at end-2025 toward the 300,000 end-2026 target and the related attach of Assist Suites.
Monitor product order growth and product backlog trajectory through 2026 versus management's call for a normal Q1 dip followed by recovery.
Watch gross/operating margin performance against tariff and memory headwinds, including evidence of pricing and mix offsets.
Track Silvus trajectory versus the $675M 2026 target and the mix between Ukraine-linked, NATO, and broader unmanned deployments.

action_items: Update MSI 2026 model assumptions for segment growth, tax rates, share count, and operating cash flow to align with call guidance.
Run channel checks on APX Next, SVX, and Assist Suite conversion by use case (dispatcher versus responder) and contract duration.
Track federal and defense program wins tied to Silvus, FedRAMP-enabled workflows, and unmanned systems demand.
open_questions: How quickly will Assist Suite seats convert from trial and early deployment into recurring paid scale across large agencies?
Can double-digit product orders hold if U.S. funding priorities shift at federal or local levels during 2026?
What level of pricing action is required to fully offset tariffs and memory inflation if cost pressure extends beyond current assumptions?
watch_next_quarter: Q1 product backlog seasonality versus management's normalization framework and order growth expectations.
Command Center growth rate and APX Next subscriber adds versus the 300,000 end-2026 target path.
Video growth mix between cloud and on-prem/hybrid deployments, including camera unit growth and software attach.
